newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assembly passes 10-cent gas tax proposal.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assembly passes 10-cent gas tax proposal.

text.p: California's Assembly approved a measure that could boost gasoline taxes in nine counties by up to 10 cents per gallon to raise $4 billion for major transportation projects, lawmakers said Wednesday.
The lower house approved Assembly Bill 595, by Assemblywoman Valerie Brown, on a vote of 42-to-32, sending the measure to the Senate for review.
The bill would allow California's Metropolitan Transportation Commission to place the gas tax proposal on ballots in nine counties in the San Francisco Bay area.

Under the measure, the commission could seek up to a 10-cent-per-gallon increase in the gasoline tax in those counties. If approved by county voters, the increase would raise up to $4 billion over 20 years to fund regional transportation projects.
The Metropolitan Transportation Commission has projected a $3.8 billion shortfall in funding for San Francisco Bay area transit projects over the next 20 years.
California motorists now pay 36 cents in gas taxes -- 18 cents to the state and 18 cents for the federal government.
